authority: Operator instruction (in-session). Logged per §9.4. Transport-layer and parser-layer changes only; no workflow logic, gate logic, artifact schema, or skill semantics altered.

problem.symptom: Phase 2 (n02_concept_refinement) failed with failure_origin='agent_body', failure_category='SKILL_FAILURE'. The reported reason was that EVERY required field was missing from concept-alignment-check's response: schema_id, run_id, topic_mapping_rationale, scope_coverage, scope_conflict_log, strategic_differentiation.
problem.misleading_diagnosis: The error pointed at the model omitting required fields. It had not. The response was FRONT-TRUNCATED: the captured text began mid-object ('{"tier3_evidence_ref":...},"CC-03":{...'), i.e. only the tail of an over-long generation was returned.
problem.root_cause_1: OUTPUT CEILING. concept-alignment-check must emit scope_coverage for every SR-xx and CC-xx element (1-3 sentence description each) plus topic_mapping_rationale for every expected outcome. This exceeded the Claude CLI's default output-token ceiling, so the generation was cut off and the CLI returned only the tail.
problem.root_cause_2: PARSER FAIL-OPEN. runner/skill_runtime.py::_extract_json_response step 1b used JSONDecoder.raw_decode() on any response starting with '{', accepting the first complete object and discarding the remainder. Its docstring claimed it 'only tolerates trailing noise after a complete valid object' - but raw_decode cannot distinguish a stray closing brace from 15KB of the real payload. On the truncated response it returned a 2-key interior fragment ({tier3_evidence_ref, notes}), which parsed 'OK' and then failed schema validation with the misleading 'required field missing' error. The real fault - an incomplete response - was never surfaced.

fixes_applied.change: Added _MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_DEFAULT = '32000' and pass an explicit env to subprocess.run with CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS set via setdefault (an operator-supplied value always wins). Added the missing 'import os'. Previously no env was passed at all, so the CLI ran at its default ceiling.
fixes_applied.constitutional_class: Transport layer only (§17.5.2 / §17.1.3). Raises an output ceiling; alters no skill semantics, no gate logic, no artifact schema.

fixes_applied.change: Step 1b now inspects the remainder after raw_decode. If the remainder opens with ',' or ':', the decoded object was a MEMBER of a larger structure whose opening was lost - the response is front-truncated - and None is returned so the caller reports INCOMPLETE_OUTPUT honestly. Trailing prose or a stray brace remains benign and the leading object is returned as before.
fixes_applied.constitutional_class: Strengthens §17.6.5 (the runtime must not silently repair Claude responses). The prior behaviour silently accepted a fragment of a malformed response, which is precisely the silent repair §17.6.5 forbids. This is a fail-closed hardening, not a relaxation.
fixes_applied.regression_guard: The narrow ','/':' discriminator was chosen deliberately over a blanket 'reject any substantive remainder' rule, which would have broken the common and benign case of a model appending a closing remark after a complete artifact.

corrected_misattribution.why_that_was_wrong: Gate g03_p06 (no_unresolved_scope_conflicts) reads docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase2_concept_refinement/concept_refinement_summary.json - the output of concept-alignment-check. topic-scope-check writes only a decision-log entry and gates nothing. defect_diagnosed_but_NOT_applied.defect: CATEGORY ERROR. The skill's anti-fabrication guard (line ~108) requires that any claim which cannot be matched to a Tier 2B scope_element_id be marked 'flagged' rather than 'in_scope' - a correct guard against §13.2/§13.9 (inferring scope from prior programme knowledge). But it conflates two different situations: (a) the call HAS thematic boundaries and this claim matches none - a real conflict; and (b) the instrument defines NO thematic boundary at all - in which case there is no element to match and there never will be. MSCA-PF is researcher-driven and topic-agnostic: it constrains eligibility, mobility, supervision, training and duration, but imposes no research-domain scope. Every research-content claim therefore fails to match, is flagged, and resolution_status is forced to 'unresolved' - unfixably, since the only way to satisfy it would be to invent Tier 2B scope elements, which §13.2 forbids.
defect_diagnosed_but_NOT_applied.secondary_defect: The skill also flagged SR-02/CC-01 on the ground that the concept declares its identity spine SYNTHETIC and 'not submittable'. That is provenance policing, not scope checking. Provenance is governed by the §12.2 validation_status, the no_unresolved_material_claims predicate, W1, and any logged §3 override. A scope checker that downgrades honestly-marked content makes transparency self-defeating.
defect_diagnosed_but_NOT_applied.status: Proposed correction written to PROPOSED_topic_scope_check_correction.md. NOT APPLIED. The repository's .claude/ directory is write-protected in the assisting session, and a skill spec is an agent instruction: a change to scope-evaluation semantics must pass through the operator explicitly rather than be applied silently by an agent. Non-blocking - it pollutes the decision log but gates nothing.
defect_diagnosed_but_NOT_applied.constitutional_note: The proposed correction is NOT a §13.7 gate weakening. It removes a check the scope gate has no jurisdiction over (provenance) and adds a disposition for constraints that do not exist (topic-agnostic instruments). Nothing goes unchecked: every provenance check remains with the authority that owns it. It must nevertheless be reviewed as a semantics change, and logged if adopted.

known_consequence_operator_should_hold_e: After the provenance/scope separation, NOTHING in the gate stack blocks synthetic data. no_unresolved_material_claims fails only on validation_status 'unresolved'; the SYN-SPINE-01 spine is 'Confirmed' + synthetic:true. W1 governs only 'assumed'. The synthetic nature of this run is therefore carried by exactly three things: the synthetic:true metadata, the logged override records, and the 'SYNTHETIC DEMO - NOT FOR SUBMISSION' watermark on the .docx. That is by design - SYN-SPINE-01 accepted precisely this trade - but it should be held consciously, not discovered later.
